distinguishing_features: Localized injection of a volatile halogenated precursor into turbine secondary/dilution air at the blade platform.
Use of an increased local oxidizing chemical potential to accelerate in-situ alpha-Al2O3 formation on an MCrAlY bond coat.
Pre-establishment of a protective oxide before CTE-mismatch shear accumulates.
MFC dosing derived from existing dilution-air pressure/flow telemetry without adding new sensors.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce early-life TBC spalling caused by slow or defective alumina-scale formation and CTE-mismatch shear during turbine thermal transients.
parsed.viable_reason: The bond coat is buried beneath the TBC and not directly exposed to dilution air, CF4 is not a credible oxygen-potential booster, and the asserted 10^4 kp increase is unsupported while halide attack would more likely degrade protective scales.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The closest art already uses feed-rate/composition changes to shift surface chemical potential, so selecting an oxidizing feed additive and dosing it through existing flow telemetry is an obvious application of that approach to the oxidation problem.
